methods: For the additional Gaussian interval diagnostics, central 90\% and 95\% intervals use standard-normal multipliers $z=1.645$ and $z=1.960$, respectively (rounded here; the archived calculations use full-precision quantiles). Prediction-interval coverage probability (PICP) is the proportion of observations within the interval, and mean prediction-interval width (MPIW) is the mean upper minus lower bound in mm\,h$^{-1}$. We report the negative-lower-bound proportion at both levels, together with diagnostic coverage for the observed wet ($y\geq0.1$~mm\,h$^{-1}$) and upper-tail ($y\geq0.574048$~mm\,h$^{-1}$, using training Q95) subsets. These diagnostics use the separate q14 five-seed Gaussian reruns summarised in Supplementary Table~\ref{supp-stab:r2minor2_intervals}.
results: Supplementary Table~\ref{supp-stab:r2minor2_intervals} reports both interval levels for the separate q14 five-seed Gaussian reruns on the same 3,939 test targets. Across the three models, mean all-sample coverage was 0.9456--0.9464 for the nominal 90\% interval and 0.9560--0.9571 for the nominal 95\% interval. The corresponding widths were 0.6526--0.6705 and 0.7776--0.7989~mm\,h$^{-1}$. For the 854 wet targets, coverage was 0.7546--0.7571 and 0.8002--0.8042, respectively; for the 238 upper-tail targets, it was 0.3958--0.4101 and 0.4941--0.5042. At both nominal levels, every lower bound was negative and every uncovered observation exceeded the upper bound. Thus, near-nominal overall 95\% coverage and above-nominal overall 90\% coverage conceal marked wet and upper-tail undercoverage. These are descriptive conditional diagnostics, not evidence of a significant model ranking.
identity: These reruns are the A2 run set in Table~\ref{tab:probabilistic_results}, rather than the complete original A1 run set. The A2 Probabilistic BiLSTM-Attention and the B Gaussian have identical saved test targets and predictive means for each of the five seeds, with small differences in the saved standard-deviation parameters (at most $1.23\times10^{-7}$~mm\,h$^{-1}$). Their agreement therefore does not constitute independent prediction evidence, despite the separate run records.
